citation.authors: Kristensen JM, Lillelund C, Kjobsted R, Birk JB, Andersen NR, Nybo L, Mellberg K, Balendran A, Richter EA, Wojtaszewski JFP
citation.title: Metformin does not compromise energy status in human skeletal muscle at rest or during acute exercise: A randomised, crossover trial

population.description: Healthy, moderately trained men in two separate crossover studies: acute (n = 9) and short-term (n = 10) metformin-exercise study (VO2 peak 53.7 +/- 1.2 and 52.3 +/- 0.9 mL/kg/min, SEM, Table 1). The model carries no training status. Age and BMI are given per study in the protocol arms (Table 1, mean +/- SEM, SD computed as SEM x sqrt(n)); no observed ranges are printed. Only the placebo day or period's values before any food or tablet are entered. The paper does not say whether the acute and short-term men overlap; 'acute (A-MES, n = 9) or a short-term (ST-MES, n = 10) study, respectively', the ST-MES added later, different n, weight and BMI, so they are entered as separate groups. The short-term study also has a pre-treatment fasting sample (-72 h, day 3) that is not entered, one fasting state per study.

protocols.name: fasting_acute
protocols.description: Acute study (A-MES, n = 9), placebo day: arrival in the morning after an overnight fast, 1 h rest, then the pre-diet blood sample (Table 2/4 row '0:00 (pre) diet') drawn before the breakfast and before the placebo tablets; arm ends at the sample (the breakfast, placebo, 4.5 h of rest and the one-leg bout are not entered). A 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample; clock hour and fast length are not printed (only 'overnight fast'), so 08:00 and 10 h are assumed. Age 24 +/- 1 SEM and BMI 24.2 +/- 0.6 SEM (Table 1, n = 9) converted to SD = SEM x sqrt(9): age 3.0, BMI 1.8.

protocols.name: fasting_short
protocols.description: Short-term study (ST-MES, n = 10), placebo period, experimental day 6: arrival in the morning after an overnight fast, blood sample at time 0 (Table 2/4 row '0:00 diet'), before the 1.5 g placebo and the breakfast; arm ends at the sample (after 3 days of placebo tablets with a controlled diet; the breakfast, 4.5 h of rest and the one-leg bout are not entered). A 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample; clock hour and fast length are not printed (only 'overnight fast'), so 08:00 and 10 h are assumed. Age 24 +/- 1 SEM and BMI 22.0 +/- 0.6 SEM (Table 1, n = 10) converted to SD = SEM x sqrt(10): age 3.16, BMI 1.90.

left_out.what: Glucose, insulin and lactate after the standardized oatmeal-and-raisins breakfast, placebo arms, 1:00 to 4:30 h (Tables 2 and 4): the breakfast is printed as about 1,800 kJ, 15% of daily energy, but not as grams of carbohydrate, fat and protein; the short-term study's standardized diet is 15% protein, 30% fat, 55% carbohydrate, but the paper does not say the day-6 breakfast follows that split

Glucose, insulin, lactate and adrenaline during the 40-min one-leg knee-extensor bout at 80% of peak work load (samples at 4:50 and 5:10 h, Tables 2 and 4) and the short-term study's 5:40, 7:10 and 9:10 h samples, placebo arms: the bout follows the unwritable breakfast by 4.5 h (whole-body VO2 1.1 +/- 0.1 L/min is printed in Table 5)
Placebo-arm resting and exercise heart rate, RER and oxygen uptake (Table 5): rest was after the breakfast, exercise is the same bout
Noradrenaline at 0:00 and through the day (Table 4)
Fasting insulin in uU/mL, HOMA-IR, 2 h glucose/insulin ratio and Matsuda index (Table 3 and text)

Table 3 fasting insulin in uU/mL of the placebo arms (3.9 acute, 4.4 short-term) is a second print of the fasting insulin of Table 2 (27 and 31 pmol/L, i.e. 4.5 and 5.2 uU/mL) that does not agree with it, and the draw is not described separately; Table 2 is entered
